_comment: Curated offline technology radar. Dates describe Ratchetry's review cadence, not upstream release guarantees. Updating entries requires an explicit research task; setup and status never access the network.

entries.name: Agent Skills
entries.relevance: Portable SKILL.md structure and progressive disclosure.
entries.rationale: Ratchetry's global Skills already use this compatible shape while retaining local security policy.
entries.next_action: Continue validating metadata, references, resources, and selective loading.

entries.name: AI Engineering from Scratch
entries.relevance: Agent engineering curriculum, evals, MCP lifecycle, and Skills packaging patterns.
entries.rationale: Useful patterns should be evaluated individually; importing a large catalog would increase context and supply-chain risk.
entries.next_action: Compare new eval and installer patterns during the next capability-quality review.

entries.name: Akita AI Memory
entries.relevance: Cross-client and team memory, typed handoffs, retention, and compatibility matrices.
entries.rationale: Ratchetry already has bounded Git/Markdown/Vault memory; automatic raw session capture and a default daemon conflict with its privacy contract.
entries.next_action: Reassess only for an optional multi-machine or team-memory backend with explicit retention.

entries.name: Claude Code Memory Setup
entries.relevance: Simple Obsidian/Graphify resume-save onboarding and Portuguese documentation.
entries.rationale: The onboarding lessons are useful, but mandatory graph tooling and automatic transcript import do not fit Ratchetry's bounded-memory policy.
entries.next_action: Use outcome-led and Portuguese onboarding patterns without copying automatic capture.

entries.name: Claude Security Agents
entries.relevance: Structured red-team findings followed by blue-team remediation and re-scan.
entries.rationale: The loop is valuable when adapted to existing agents with a human gate and no automatic installs or commits.
entries.next_action: Benchmark Ratchetry's security-hardening workflow against representative vulnerable fixtures.

entries.name: Claude Maestro
entries.relevance: Worktree isolation, ownership, status files, and integration coordination.
entries.rationale: Embedding a tmux multi-session orchestrator would expand Ratchetry beyond workspace setup and introduce cooperative coordination risk.
entries.next_action: Reuse ownership and integration-owner guidance only; revisit orchestration if user demand and benchmarks justify it.

entries.name: AIWorkspace
entries.relevance: Canonical workspace configuration, source/hash lockfiles, and editor adapters.
entries.rationale: Provenance and export patterns fit; automatic package-time config and hook writes do not.
entries.next_action: Compare lock and collision semantics before designing third-party Skill import.

entries.name: Microsoft Skills
entries.relevance: Large selective catalog, plugin packaging, agents, and MCP configurations.
entries.rationale: Selective discovery can inform Ratchetry, while loading an entire catalog would cause context and review debt.
entries.next_action: Inspect only Skills tied to a concrete user goal and pass them through a future import review.

entries.name: OpenAI Plugins
entries.relevance: Current packaging direction for Skills, MCP servers, and apps.
entries.rationale: Export adapters may improve distribution, but Ratchetry should keep one canonical source and wait for stable compatibility evidence.
entries.next_action: Review manifest and validation changes before a plugin-export experiment.

entries.name: OpenAI Skills (legacy repository)
entries.rationale: The repository points users to OpenAI Plugins; it is retained only as migration context.
entries.next_action: Do not build new integration against the legacy repository.

entries.name: Model Context Protocol Registry
entries.rationale: Read-only discovery may help later, but preview APIs and third-party supply-chain risk rule out automatic install or enablement.
entries.next_action: Recheck API stability before designing an offline-cached search and risk-review command.

entries.name: skills.sh
entries.relevance: Discovery index for portable Agent Skills, current activity, and source repositories.
entries.rationale: Useful as a lead generator only. Install counts and third-party audit badges are not sufficient trust or product-fit evidence.
entries.next_action: Review only goal-relevant candidates through license, provenance, permission, behavior-eval, and rollback gates.

entries.name: Matt Pocock Engineering Skills
entries.relevance: Vertical-slice TDD, disciplined diagnosis, domain vocabulary, and composable engineering workflows.
entries.rationale: Ratchetry adopted the behavior-first TDD and evidence-first debugging patterns in newly written native Skills; it does not subscribe to or bulk-copy the upstream catalog.
entries.next_action: Measure routing precision and contribution quality before adapting any additional pattern.

entries.name: Superpowers
entries.relevance: Systematic debugging, red-green-refactor, and evidence-before-completion disciplines across coding clients.
entries.rationale: Ratchetry adopted selected process patterns in native Skills while excluding the complete framework, automatic orchestration, and optional remote visual telemetry.
entries.next_action: Benchmark the two adapted Skills; keep all other upstream capabilities opt-in research candidates.

entries.name: TypeSafe Jev
entries.relevance: Fast typed probabilistic decisions for bounded classification, routing, scoring, and guardrail questions.
entries.rationale: Promising for narrow closed-set judgments, but it is a hosted early-access service: inputs leave the machine, credentials and spend are required, model behavior can change, and vendor claims need local calibration evidence.
entries.next_action: Run a synthetic/public-data benchmark against deterministic routing and existing models; pin a version, validate thresholds, and retain a local fallback before any trial.

entries.name: Agent2Agent Protocol
entries.relevance: Interoperability, capability discovery, and long-running task exchange between independent agent services.
entries.rationale: The standard is credible, but Ratchetry is a local operating layer rather than a hosted multi-agent runtime; adding A2A now would expand product scope and attack surface without a validated user journey.
entries.next_action: Track the specification and authentication model; reconsider only for a concrete cross-service handoff use case.

entries.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions
entries.relevance: Common vocabulary for agent, workflow, plan, tool, retrieval, and memory traces.
entries.rationale: The vocabulary can improve optional benchmark evidence, but the agent conventions are still in development and Ratchetry must not add always-on telemetry or content capture.
entries.next_action: Map only aggregate local benchmark fields to stable conventions after they mature; keep exporters and content capture out of the core.
